newsitem.title: USA: US VIEW: Australia, NZ equities could be included in fund.
newsitem.headline: US VIEW: Australia, NZ equities could be included in fund.

text.p: Melbourne-based National Mutual Funds Management (NMFM), which controls the Ernst Global Asset Allocation Fund, may soon allocate five to six percent of its investment portfolio to Australian and New Zealand equities.

Australia and New Zealand, excluded from global asset allocation weightings since the fund's launch in July, represent increasingly attractive opportunities on a global scale as the fund continues to review and diversify investments, according to the New York adviser to the soon-to-be US$25 million fund.

Robert Bonelli, executive vice president of Ernst & Co and president of its mutual funds management arm, Ernst Asset Management, said the fund currently divides its equity investments fairly evenly between the UK (9.2 percent), France (9.6 percent) and Germany (10.2 percent) with Hong Kong at 15.3 percent, Japan 8.2 percent and the U.S. 6.8 percent.
The remainder of the fund, which targets U.S. investors, is spread across U.S. cash and bonds.
Bonelli told reporters here the conservative, long-term capital appreciation fund was underweight in Japan and yet to invest in Australia or New Zealand.
But Richard Greenfield, chief investment allocation officer at NMFM, believes Australia and New Zealand's equity markets merit a closer look, according to Bonelli.

Bonelli said the global allocations which are reviewed weekly by Greenfield and on a real time basis by portfolio managers in the countries in which the fund invests, may be diverted from the 39 percent weighting in U.S. bonds -- mostly short to mid term maturities.
But some "could come from pulling back from Germany or pulling back from the UK" where macro-economic conditions may be changing.
"The allocation process (for all the weightings) could change next week," Bonelli said.
Japan's underweight position may take six to 12 months to turn around, he added.
The fund, the third global investment fund distributed by Ernst's World Funds family is sub-advised by NMFM whose parent National Mutual Holdings is 51 percent owned by the Paris-based AXA Group.
AXA, including NMFM's US$18 billion, manages about US$300 billion worldwide. AXA is also a majority holder of the Equitible Life Insurance Co of the U.S.
National Mutual provided $US5 million in seed money to the fund.
Funds under management are expected to be about US$25 million in the next 10 days following a US$10 million injection from AXA.

As distributors of the fund, Ernst Funds Management has signed about 15,000 registered broker/dealer representatives around the United States whose firms have agreed to sell the funds to their clients.
To maintain its conservative position, the fund invests only in large cap equities, triple A rated or sovereign debt and hedges exposure to global currencies back to the U.S. dollar.
"U.S. investors are a little concerned about currency risk," said Bonelli. He said Eastern European and South American markets did not play a role in the fund to date.
